subject: Discovery recap: model evaluation next steps, recommended models, and prompt harvest
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Oliver Zhang <oliver.zhang@curelytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 15:08:00 -0500
Subject: Discovery recap: model evaluation next steps, recommended models, and prompt harvest

Hi Oliver —

Thanks again for Friday’s demo and the time to walk through Curelytics’ ingestion flows and the clinical QA workflows. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can scope a short model-fit proof of concept that focuses on your triage + QA use case: 

Recap (what we heard)
- Primary goal: surface incorrect labels and highlight candidate edits in medical claims and provider notes before human review.
- Data: mix of structured claims and free-text notes; monthly volume ~1.2M events, peak latency target for triage suggestions ~400ms for interactive review.
- Constraints: HIPAA + contractual retention rules (30–90 days for raw extracts), need for audit logs.

Our recommended short-list for the POC (we'll run benchmarks on your prompt set):
- Llama 2 13B Chat (v2, instruction-tuned) — great balance of instruction-following and low latency when served quantized.
- Falcon 40B Instruct — strong few-shot accuracy for complex extraction tasks (we'll test latency envelope).
- Redwood-13B-instruct-quant — our Redwood-curated variant that often hits best cost/latency tradeoffs for chat-style QA when KV caching is effective.

Attached: a simple prompt_schema.csv that shows the CSV format we prefer for prompt ingestion and a redaction_checklist.pdf with initial guidance.

Ask / next steps
1) Can you share a sample set of 150–250 representative prompts/queries (real examples preferred, redacted where needed)? We primarily need: typical queries, 12–15 edge-case examples, and a handful (~10) that include PHI/PII so we can test redaction efficacy. Please use the schema attached.
2) Please indicate whether Curelytics prefers: a) upload to our secure S3 intake link (we'll provide a presigned URL), b) share via your SFTP, or c) add to the Drive folder we created (link below).
3) Any hard constraints on tokens-per-request, or explicit blocker patterns (e.g., do not send raw MRNs) we should enforce before ingestion?

Benchmarks & timeline
- We'll run initial model benching within 5 business days of receiving the prompt sample and a small labeled validation set. Expect a one-page summary with per-model accuracy, latency at p95, and cost-per-1k tokens.

Security & deployment note
- If HIPAA is required, we’ll propose Redwood Private (VPC) for the pilot; Marissa is copied to scope controls and redaction guidance.

Oliver — if this looks good I’ll open a HubSpot action (DEAL-8921) and Marissa will follow up on security intake. Thanks again —

—Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0127

Attachments: prompt_schema.csv (CSV), redaction_checklist.pdf (PDF)
Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-eval-benchmarks
From: Oliver Zhang <oliver.zhang@curelytics.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: Curelytics Data Team <data@curelytics.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 08:04:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: model evaluation next steps, recommended models, and prompt harvest

Hi Naomi —

Appreciate the clear recap and the quick turnaround. This aligns with what we discussed. A few clarifying points before we share data: 

- HIPAA: yes, PHI is in scope. We cannot share raw patient identifiers outside a covered environment. We would prefer the Redwood Private option for the POC unless you can guarantee a BAA and SOC2 Type II controls on hosted.
- Prompt set: we can assemble ~200 examples. We have two question buckets — claim-normalization queries and free-text QA prompts. We will include ~15 edge cases (ambiguous abbreviations, merged sentences, and truncated notes).
- Redaction: can you confirm whether your redaction_checklist includes guidance for pseudonymization vs. full token removal? We have some business cases where masked but linkable IDs are needed internally.

We prefer option (a) presigned S3 upload; please send the link and the retention policy. Also please share the benchmark template and what a labeled validation set should look like (format, sample size).

Thanks — planning team will aim to deliver the prompt set and a 200-record labeled validation sample by EOD next Wednesday (Dec 7).

Regards,
Oliver Zhang
Head of Data Platforms | Curelytics
oliver.zhang@curelytics.com | (617) 555-8891

Hi Oliver —

Thanks — quick notes from a security/CS perspective: 

1) Redaction guidance: the checklist we attached includes two levels: 
   - Remove: direct identifiers (MRN, SSN, full DOB when not needed), phone numbers, email addresses.
   - Pseudonymize: internal IDs and provider names if you need linkability for downstream QA workflows — we recommend HMAC-based pseudonymization with an internal key kept on your side.

2) Intake & retention: If you use the presigned S3 route we’ll provide a bucket with a 14-day auto-delete lifecycle (configurable). For the pilot we recommend keeping working artifacts (prompts + labeled validation set) for 30 days. We will not retain raw unredacted copies in hosted unless you opt in.

3) Private deployment / BAA: Redwood Private is the tightest route. If you need a BAA we’ll loop Legal — we’ve executed BAAs with other health customers before.

4) Format for labeled validation set: CSV with columns: prompt_id, prompt_text, expected_label, confidence_band, note. 200 records is perfect for initial comparisons.

I’ll open the secure intake + a short security questionnaire for your legal/security contact (DocuSign link below). Ben — looping you for commercial/next-step cadence.

Best,
Marissa
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Related: security questionnaire: https://docusign.com/sq/secure-CURE-8921

Oliver —

Thanks for the heads-up and for committing to the prompt set + 200-record labeled sample. Proposed mutual action plan and asks from our side: 

1) Naomi/Marissa to deliver: presigned S3 intake link, quick-run benchmark template, and estimated scope of Redwood Private (controls list) by EOD Tuesday.
2) Curelytics to deliver: prompt set (200) + labeled validation (200) by EOD Wed Dec 7.
3) Commercial: I'll draft a short pilot agreement (30-day pilot, two-week kickoff, pilot fees waived pending evaluation) and upload to HubSpot for signatures. Please indicate the final procurement contact and authorize a PO, or if you prefer DocuSign flow.

HubSpot (DEAL-8921): https://hubspot.company/contacts/DEAL-8921
